title: Étienne Sinotte
text:
¡Bienvenides!
Soy candidato al doctorado en el Departamento de Ciencia Política de la Universidad McGill. Trabajo principalmente en política comparada, con un enfoque regional sobre América Latina.
Mi investigación aborda los vínculos entre el desplazamiento, el extractivismo y la ciudadanía democrática en América Latina. En particular, pregunto cómo la presencia o la ausencia del Estado determina quién es gobernado, y por quién, en sus periferias extractivas y criminales. Este proyecto surge de un trabajo de campo previo en Perú sobre la gobernanza colaborativa, que primero llamó mi atención sobre quiénes ocupan el lugar allí donde el Estado se retira, y sobre las redes que llenan ese espacio.
Tengo una maestría (M. Sc.) en Ciencia Política por la Universidad de Montreal y una licenciatura en Estudios Políticos Aplicados por la Universidad de Sherbrooke.

title: Étienne Sinotte
text:
Bienvenue!
Je suis doctorant au Département de science politique de l’Université McGill. Je travaille principalement en politique comparée, avec un focus régional sur l’Amérique latine.
Ma recherche porte sur les rapports entre le déplacement forcé, l’extractivisme et les régimes de citoyenneté en Amérique latine. Je m’intéresse particulièrement à la manière dont la présence (ou l’absence) de l’État détermine qui est gouverné, et par qui, dans les périphéries où s’exercent l’extraction et la gouvernance criminelle. Ce projet suit dans les pas d’une recherche précédente menée au Pérou sur la gouvernance collaborative, qui a d’abord attiré mon attention sur ce qui arrive lorsque l’État se retire, et sur les réseaux qui comblent ce vide.
Je détiens une maîtrise (M. Sc.) en science politique de l’Université de Montréal et un baccalauréat en études politiques appliquées de l’Université de Sherbrooke.

title: Research
text: Examines why states recognize some forms of displacement (climate-, development-, and persecution-led) while rendering others legally invisible, and what this reveals about democratic quality in Latin America.

title: Research
text:
Working Papers

Making Collaborative Governance Work in Contexts of State Weakness and Disengagement: Peru’s Indigenous COVID-19 Command (Under Review)
Peru’s Indigenous COVID Commands (ICCs) varied widely in effectiveness, and La Convención’s ICC outperformed others despite its peripheral status due to a pre-existing legacy of health collaboration and unusually strong NGO involvement. These NGOs compensated for chronic state disengagement by sustaining coordination and mediating between the state and indigenous communities, producing a hybrid of community-led and symbolic coproduction that yielded comparatively high vaccination rates.

title: Research
text:
Chapters

Definitions of northern/rural/remote/peripheric communities in Canada, in the Research Companion to the Periphery and Peripheral Regions: Concepts, Diagnosis, Dilemmas, edited by Jerzy Banski, 2025.
(with François Brouard, Natalya Brown, and Manuel Litalien)
Inconsistent definitions for northern, rural, and remote Canadian communities lead to oversimplified classifications that ignore regional diversity and result in poorly tailored public policies and a philanthropic sector which neglects smaller communities in favor of urban centers. A nuanced, multi-factor approach is essential to accurately identify community needs and ensure the equitable delivery of social programs.

title: Étienne Sinotte
text:
Welcome!
I am a PhD candidate in the Department of Political Science at McGill University. I primarily work in comparative politics, with a regional focus on Latin America.
My research examines the relationship between displacement, extractivism, criminal governance, and democratic citizenship in Latin America. In particular, I investigate how the presence or absence of the state shapes who is governed, and by whom, at its extractive and criminal margins. This project grows out of earlier fieldwork in Peru on collaborative governance, which first drew my attention to who steps in where the state withdraws, and to the networks that fill that space.
I hold an MSc in Political Science from the Université de Montréal, and a BA in Applied Political Studies from the Université de Sherbrooke.
